Enceladus in Silhouette (NASA Astronomy Picture of the Day)

One of our Solar System's most tantalizing worlds, Enceladus is backlit by the Sun in this Cassini spacecraft image from November 1, 2009. The dramatic illumination reveals the plumes that continuously spew into space from the south pole of Saturn's 500 kilometer diameter moon.

Source: NASA APOD (5 Nov 2026).
https://science.nasa.gov/image-article/apod-2026-november-5-enceladus-in-silhouette/

Yesterday's answer: Mercury, 88.0 days per orbit (NASA Planetary Fact Sheet).

Today's quiz ⚖️ Which of these planets is the most massive?

Answer tomorrow.

The Sun you see is 8 minutes old

Step two: the Sun. The average distance between Earth and the Sun is so useful that astronomers gave it its own unit, the astronomical unit, fixed by the IAU in 2012 at 149,597,870.7 kilometers. Light covers it in 499 seconds. That is 8 minutes and 19 seconds. The Sun you see is always the Sun of eight minutes ago.

Source: NASA.
